sections.title: Reading Comprehension · Passage B
sections.intro: Read “I Am Vertical” and answer questions 11–14. A vocabulary note follows the poem.

passage.title: I Am Vertical
passage.credit: —Sylvia Plath · from Uncollected Poems (1965), Turret Books

lines.text: But I would rather be horizontal.
I am not a tree with my root in the soil
Sucking up minerals and motherly love
So that each March I may gleam into leaf,
Nor am I the beauty of a garden bed
Attracting my share of Ahs and spectacularly painted,
Unknowing I must soon unpetal.
Compared with me, a tree is immortal
And a flower-head not tall, but more startling,
And I want the one’s longevity and the other’s daring.
Tonight, in the infinitesimal¹ light of the stars,
The trees and flowers have been strewing their cool odors.
I walk among them, but none of them are noticing.
Sometimes I think that when I am sleeping
I must most perfectly resemble them—
Thoughts gone dim.
It is more natural to me, lying down.
Then the sky and I are in open conversation,
And I shall be useful when I lie down finally:
Then the trees may touch me for once, and the flowers
have time for me.
¹ infinitesimal — very small

questions.explanation: A flower that “unpetals” loses its petals soon after blooming. The invented verb highlights how brief its beauty is.

questions.prompt: Lines 11 through 13 reveal the narrator’s awareness of

choices.text: the limited time people exist on earth
the unexpected changes that affect one’s life
her anxiety over the shifting of seasons
her insignificance in the eyes of nature

questions.explanation: As the speaker walks among trees and flowers beneath the stars, she notices that none of them notice her. Nature’s indifference makes her feel small.

questions.prompt: In lines 14 through 16, the narrator suggests that

choices.text: consciousness is a barrier to connecting with nature
nature’s ability to impress surpasses human’s imagination
the future depends on natural forces beyond human control
nature’s cruelty causes one to feel helpless

questions.explanation: The speaker thinks she most resembles trees and flowers when sleeping, with her thoughts dimmed. Ordinary human consciousness seems to separate her from nature.

questions.explanation: The speaker says she wants the tree’s longevity and the flower’s daring and wishes to connect with them, expressing envy of their qualities.
